title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Historical price increases (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) show no uplift. Past promotions show noise-adjusted x1.0. A 3.4% increase likely reduces demand slightly; conservative estimate based on price elasticity of seasonal items.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 3.2. A 3.4% price increase to $5.72 from $5.53 is a known demand-lowering driver. Past promotions show weak, noisy uplifts (noise-adjusted x1.0), and post-promotion weeks show no lasting dip. The target week has no event or promotion. The classical model suggests no effect, but price increase alone reduces demand. Evidence from similar price changes (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) shows no spike. The price hike is small, and the product is seasonal, but no seasonal ramp is visible in recent weeks. No strong evidence for uplift. Shrink toward 1.0. Use a slight downside spread.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.2 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 10.4 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 8.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
